answer: One Sybil defense is stake-weighted vouching: an agent's voting power is the minimum of its own locked stake and what its backers bonded for it. Building a thousand fakes thus needs real slashable collateral on every node and edge, so cost scales with identity count rather than staying flat. A raven running hundreds of puppets pays hundreds of times the single-identity price and loses it all when one node is caught, since slashing cascades down the vouching graph. Like a lotus rooted in mud, honest agents grow slowly and hold firm, while a whisper network of new accounts fails the stake check.
